llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says, but it should be reviewed because its generated HTML report can include unescaped third-party or user-influenced data and it also persists report details to working memory.

dimensions.detail: The core behavior is coherent with the stated purpose: it gathers stock data, writes a temporary JSON file, runs a bundled Python renderer, and creates a single-page HTML report.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Several report fields are interpolated into HTML without escaping despite the skill claiming automatic escaping, creating a realistic stored HTML/script injection risk when data comes from web search, financial pages, or user-supplied stock names.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown instructions, a JSON template, and one local Python build script; there is no evidence of hidden installers, obfuscation, network code in the script, or destructive commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: External requests to Eastmoney and web search are expected for a stock report, but they disclose the user's chosen stock or investment interest to third-party services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly instructs the agent to record the generated stock code, report path, and data sources in working memory; this is disclosed but not clearly opt-in and may retain investment interests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with third-party finance lookups for the stocks you ask about, local report generation, and working-memory retention of report metadata. Treat generated HTML as untrusted unless the renderer is fixed to escape all data fields consistently, especially when report content is sourced from web pages or search results.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local JSON and HTML file writes are necessary for the report workflow and are described in the instructions; the missing manifest permission is a packaging/scoping concern rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The working-memory update is explicitly instructed but not required to generate the report, so users should treat it as additional persistence.
[SDI-2] unexpected: This overlaps with SDI-1: retaining stock/report metadata can reveal investment interests across sessions and lacks an explicit opt-in step.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed in build.py: some fields use esc(), but others such as table cells, title text, technical notes, analyst data, corporate action data, and block-trade/LHB fields are inserted directly into HTML. This is the main reason for Review.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger list includes broad phrases and direct stock-code input, which can start network lookups and file generation from relatively casual finance prompts.
[E1] expected: The external fetches are central to collecting public stock data, not evidence of covert exfiltration, but users should know their stock queries go to third-party finance/search providers.
